content:
Maya (support): Opening thread for an escalated 429/limiter problem reported by ACME. They saw a sudden spike in 429s after our limiter deploy and have shared traces showing X-RateLimit-Remaining going negative.

Jon (customer-success): ACME reported the issue at ~2026-03-15T11:12Z. They are on Dedicated and said their webhook ingestion caused large concurrent bursts. They're blocked for one region.

Maya (support): Example response headers they pasted: 
`HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`
`X-RateLimit-Limit: 600`
`X-RateLimit-Remaining: -1`
`X-RateLimit-Reset: 1678890000`

OpsBot: deploy:rate-limiter-config v2.4.1 -> prod (triggered by rachel) at 2026-03-15T11:11:13Z :rocket:

Sanjay (eng-runtime): Looking at the v2.4.1 limiter change. We added an "auto-burst" Lua path that fast-applies extra tokens when batch_size>0 and a redis-lua optimization. Pulling the exact script now.

Sanjay (eng-runtime): Scrubbed/sanitized snippet we deployed:
```lua
local key = KEYS[1]
local now = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local tokens = tonumber(redis.call('GET', key) or 0)
local refill = math.floor((now - tonumber(redis.call('HGET', key, 'last') or now)) * RATE_PER_SEC)
tokens = tokens + refill
local take = tonumber(ARGV[2])
if take > tokens and ARGV[3] == 'burst' then
  tokens = tokens - (take * -1)  -- attempt to allow burst by negating
end
redis.call('SET', key, tokens)
return tokens
```

Sanjay (eng-runtime): That `tokens = tokens - (take * -1)` is obviously wrong: it writes negative values into Redis when take>tokens. Our header logic exposes raw values, hence negative X-RateLimit-Remaining.

Rachel (prodops): Redis inspection: many keys under `limiter:acct:*` have negative integers like `-128` and `-1024`. Redis CPU jumped ~30% due to extra work.

Eli (eng-sre): Negative values get treated as consumed tokens in aggregation which made things look exhausted globally. We need immediate rollback + scrub.

Maya (support): Customer wants ETA and mitigation steps — they're losing traffic.

Sanjay (eng-runtime): Initiating rollback of rate-limiter-config v2.4.1. Also enabling a maintenance bypass for Dedicated accounts and preparing a clamp script to fix keys.

OpsBot: rollback:rate-limiter-config v2.4.1 -> prod (initiated by Sanjay) at 2026-03-15T11:19:02Z

Eli (eng-sre): Please share the clamp script before you run it. We'll run it throttled to avoid a Redis thundering herd.

Sanjay (eng-runtime): Draft clamp script:
```bash
# scan and clamp negatives
redis-cli --scan --pattern 'limiter:acct:*' | while read k; do
  v=$(redis-cli GET "$k")
  if [ "${v#-}" != "$v" ]; then
    # value is negative
    redis-cli SET "$k" 0
  fi
done
```

Eli (eng-sre): Good start. Use EVALSHA for atomic clamp and add sleep to limit 200 keys/sec. I'll prepare a throttled runner.

Rachel (prodops): Bypass enabled for Dedicated tenants. I posted a notice to customers and raised alert sensitivity for 429s/5xx.

Maya (support): ACME reports partial recovery after rollback and bypass; older long-lived connections still see intermittent 429s but new requests mostly succeed. They asked for a root cause summary.

Sanjay (eng-runtime): Root cause: a bad arithmetic operation in Lua burst path wrote negative token counts under concurrency. High-rate webhook bursts exposed it and negative tokens propagated through aggregates causing widespread throttling.

Eli (eng-sre): Immediate post-incident actions: revert code permanently until tests added; run scrub job throttled; add monitoring for negative limiter values; implement canary rollouts for limiter changes.

Jon (customer-success): ACME wants confirmation that their buckets were reset and a timestamp for the clamp operation. We'll provide scrub CSV.

Sanjay (eng-runtime): Running scrub in batches of 200 keys/s. Will emit CSV rows key,old_value,new_value,timestamp. Starting job now.

OpsBot: job:clamp-limiter-keys started by Sanjay at 2026-03-15T11:23:30Z (batch 0/estimated 12k keys)

Sanjay (eng-runtime): Local repro I used: run redis locally and hammer endpoints to cause bursts. Example:
```bash
for i in {1..1000}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer test" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?acct=test&len=1" &
done
wait
```
Inspect headers: X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-BurstUsed, X-RateLimit-Reset.

Eli (eng-sre): Added INC-2026-03-15-limiter-burst to the board. Responsibilities: Sanjay (codefix), Eli (infra), Rachel (comms), Maya (support).

Maya (support): Customer wants three deliverables: confirmation their limiter keys were clamped, succinct root cause, and timeline for a safe fix. I told them a postmortem in 48 hours.

Sanjay (eng-runtime): Opened PR with fix and added unit + integration tests against redis-mock: https://stash.redwood/infr/repo/pull/324. Tests cover negative write prevention and a burst integration test.

Rachel (prodops): Prod deploy checklist for the fix: canary 10% for 1 hour, key-value histogram monitor, gradual ramp, clear rollback path.

Eli (eng-sre): Long-term mitigations: implement a `max_negative_tokens` safety clamp in runtime (no writes below -100), alert on any negative keys, and scheduled audits for limiter key distributions.

Sanjay (eng-runtime): Status: rollback done, scrub job running (batch 3/60 at time of last update), bypass enabled for Dedicated. Will attach scrub CSV and PR link to the incident ticket when complete.

OpsBot: job:clamp-limiter-keys completed at 2026-03-15T11:48:32Z (12,234 keys processed, 1,842 clamped). CSV uploaded to s3://redwood-incident-archives/1772002113/scrub-results.csv

Maya (support): Drafted customer note and will attach scrub output + timeline. Customer acknowledged service restored and asked for canary alerts.

Jon (customer-success): I'll be primary contact for the canary window. Please ping when canary starts so I can notify ACME.

Eli (eng-sre): Scheduling post-incident review tomorrow 09:00 PT to go over test gaps, canary gating, and internal runbook for limiter incidents.

Sanjay (eng-runtime): Quick tip: when debugging negative X-RateLimit-Remaining, check for recent limiter config deploys and inspect `limiter:*` keys for negative values before assuming client behavior.

Rachel (prodops): Continuing cleanup and will update INC ticket with final metrics. Closing the incident Slack thread for operations; we'll keep the INC ticket open until postmortem is complete.

Maya (support): Thanks team ":white_check_mark:" — sending customer follow-up now.

Eli (eng-sre): Good job all. Postmortem will include remediation plan and timeline.
